title: How failing fifth-grade math made him love it
summary: He retells the conditional promotion, mastering fractions, and algebra and geometry as arithmetic that gave him a year of college math.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So you got wrapped up in Math. It just so happened that you got interested. Now tell me, what got you so interested in it, Foots?

Well, it happened accidentally. In the Fifth Grade I failed in Math. So they had a plan in the school at that time, they'd put you in the next class on condition, and the condition was if you kept up with the next class, they wouldn't put you back. Well, man, I thought to myself, I believe I've got to be dumb. Here I didn't have nothin' to do but study, and here I was failing -- and that Fifth Grade Math must have been easy. So when they put me over in the Sixth Grade, for the fear of being put back, I studied Sixth Grade Math so hard and got it so good that I didn't have to take the final exam. I made A's in all the pre-examinations. And it so happened I remembered that Sixth Grade Math is fractions. And I found out early in life, if you study hard, the test don't mean nothin' -- because if you've got it in your mind, it's easy.

So that's how I fell in love with Math. So when I went through high school... I don't know what happened in my Seven and Eighth Grade. But when I went to high school, my first Math teacher in Algebra pointed out to us that Algebra was nothing but Arithmetic in algebraic form. Well, I

figured I had my arithmetic, so this thing won't be nothin'. So I scooted through Algebra. And when we got to Geometry, the same thing happened. They said, "Geometry is just Arithmetic all over again, but you're dealing with lines and angles and whatnot."

And that's how I fell in love with it. And there was four or five guys in school... We had teachers that would teach us these different subjects in Math. When I finished high school, I had one year of college math to my credit. But later on in life, I found out what it meant to me. Because it made music easy... It made every endeavor I went into easy, because I got ideas from that Math thing, and they all worked! And that's why I harp on that. If you get Math, whatever you go into, it will make it easy, because...
So that's one of your advices to young people.
Okay, now what else is there? Is there anything else?
